description: Summary of the full exploration findings for C:\pics. This JSON is the sole handoff material given to the downstream Stage 2 agent, which will design and execute the full pipeline based on it without re-exploring the raw data.

boston_university.content_note: Flat directory. Real photographs (high-resolution campus/event JPEGs) mixed with UI screenshots (small PNGs). Filenames indicate origin from the Boston University website. About 12% are PNG (307/2722), many of which are UI elements.

digital_domain.content_note: Flat directory. CG/VFX studio images. Filenames contain Chinese URL-encoded characters and MXF still-frame references. Very likely a mix of film stills, renders, and real photographs.

kpmg_forensic.content_note: Small flat dataset. Filenames indicate 'html' screenshots and article illustrations. High near-duplicate rate (9 pairs out of 60 sampled). Very likely documents/screenshots.

m_immobilier.content_note: All JPEG. Real-estate photos, naming pattern consistent with the centris.ca website. Each listing is named with a numbering system (e.g. _1.jpg through _27.jpg). Very likely real interior/exterior property photos.

maior_capital.content_note: Italian real-estate investment firm. Contains both real property photos and floor plans (filenames include 'pianta', 'planimetria'). Filenames indicate multilingual content (German/English/Italian).

roland_berger.content_note: Management consulting firm. About 50% PNG. Filenames indicate infographics, chart captions, user-flow diagrams, and article illustrations. Low colorfulness suggests a large amount of text-dense infographic content.

tara_guerard.content_note: Personal/artist blog archive. Filename timestamps span the 2009-2020s. Blog-style content: fashion, people, events, Cadillac cars. Very likely real photographs mixed with some design/blog graphics.

thema-med.content_note: Medical device consulting firm. Filenames indicate regulatory/compliance themes. Many PNGs are likely infographics/presentation slides. 2 near-duplicate pairs found.

truro_school.content_note: The dominant dataset (59% of the total). Content uploaded via the school website's WordPress. Photos of students, choir, events, sports, campus. Real photographs with very high diversity. PNGs are very likely graphics/thumbnails.

tuv_rheinland.content_note: TUV certification/consulting firm. 56% PNG. Filenames are long and contain German phrases. Very likely a large number of certification-themed infographics, charts, and illustrations. Low colorfulness suggests predominantly monochrome/document-type content.

ul_solutions.content_note: UL safety-standards/e-commerce platform. Path naming is Drupal-style. Mix of product photos, homepage banner images, and generic stock imagery. 1 near-duplicate pair found (localized versions of the same image).

heuristic_quality_assessment.summary: Heuristic content-type guesses based on a 60-image sample per dataset, using sharpness (mean Sobel gradient), brightness, and colorfulness (Hasler-Susstrunk metric). These are only noisy, rough estimates.

boston_university.guess: Suspected text/document type -- high sharpness plus low colorfulness suggests a mix of text/UI elements and real photographs

digital_domain.guess: Suspected monochrome or low-saturation content -- low brightness, moderate sharpness, possibly film stills/VFX shots

kpmg_forensic.guess: Suspected real photographs or renders -- high sharpness, moderate color

m_immobilier.guess: Suspected real-estate interiors -- moderate sharpness, colorfulness on the low side (due to indoor lighting)

maior_capital.guess: Suspected real photographs or renders -- both sharpness and color are decent, consistent with property photos mixed with some floor plans

roland_berger.guess: Suspected text/document type -- extremely high sharpness plus extremely low colorfulness = infographic/text-dense content

tara_guerard.guess: Mixed/uncertain -- blog content spans photographs, graphic design, and collages

thema-med.guess: Suspected real photographs or renders -- mix of presentation graphics and some photographs

truro_school.guess: Mixed/uncertain -- school photos should be real photographs, but may include some graphics

tuv_rheinland.guess: Suspected text/document type -- extremely low colorfulness, high sharpness, suggests infographics/diagrams

ul_solutions.guess: Suspected text/document type -- product photos mixed with graphics

heuristic_quality_assessment.caution: The colorfulness metric can misclassify evenly lit indoor real photographs (neutral tones) as 'text-type'. The sharpness metric captures edge energy, and both text and crisp photographs score high on it. These are all imperfect heuristic signals.

sample_statistics.per_dataset_sampling: 60 images sampled per dataset, drawn from a random shuffle of the flat collection (all datasets are single-level directories)
sample_statistics.read_failures: Zero read failures across 660 sampled images (60x11). All JPEG and PNG files opened successfully with PIL.
sample_statistics.corrupted_files: No corrupted files detected in the sample. A small number of GIF/BMP files exist based on filenames but were not sampled. Overall corruption rate appears very low.

timing.time_per_image_basic_heuristics: 0.15-0.42 seconds per image on CPU (Intel UHD 770, single-threaded PIL + numpy Sobel gradient)
timing.time_per_image_range: Depends on image resolution: small images (300x300) take about 0.05s, large images (6720x4480) take about 0.8s
timing.notes: Timing includes: PIL open+load, resize to max 640px, Sobel gradient sharpness, brightness, colorfulness, dhash (8x9). Does not include FFT or model inference.

near_duplicate_and_diversity.dhash_method: 8x9 difference hash (64-bit), Hamming distance <=4 treated as a near duplicate, checked within a sliding window (window of 30 for 60-image samples, window of 50 for 200-image samples)

datasets_with_duplicates.kpmg_forensic: 29 near-duplicate pairs out of 80 images (36% duplicate rate) -- the highest so far. All 80 images were scanned. These are screenshots of the same HTML page in different states.
datasets_with_duplicates.thema-med: 21 near-duplicate pairs out of a 200-image sample (10.5% duplicate rate) -- presentation slides with slightly different layouts
datasets_with_duplicates.tuv_rheinland: 5 near-duplicate pairs out of a 200-image sample (2.5% duplicate rate) -- localized versions of the same image
datasets_with_duplicates.boston_university: 1 near-duplicate pair out of a 200-image sample -- very likely similar UI screenshots
datasets_with_duplicates.ul_solutions: 1 near-duplicate pair out of a 200-image sample (0.5%) -- variants of a multilingual banner image
datasets_with_duplicates.digital_domain: 0 duplicate pairs -- all unique in the sample
datasets_with_duplicates.m_immobilier: 0 duplicate pairs -- all unique in the sample
datasets_with_duplicates.maior_capital: 0 duplicate pairs -- all unique in the sample
datasets_with_duplicates.roland_berger: 0 duplicate pairs -- all unique in the sample
datasets_with_duplicates.tara_guerard: 0 duplicate pairs -- all unique in the sample
datasets_with_duplicates.truro_school: 0 duplicate pairs out of a 200-image scan -- content diversity is very likely high

near_duplicate_and_diversity.diversity_notes: Most datasets show a 0% near-duplicate rate in their sample. The datasets with a high duplicate rate (kpmg_forensic, thema-med) are themselves small, and the whole dataset's content is very likely fairly similar throughout. Deduplication is essential for kpmg_forensic and thema-med; the rest naturally have relatively high diversity.

environment_and_capabilities.ram: Available (not precisely measured, but sufficient for PIL processing of 60 images)
environment_and_capabilities.torch_bench: A simple tensor operation took about 412ms (including import overhead; actual MobileCLIP inference will take far longer than this)
environment_and_capabilities.open_clip_torch: 3.3.0, available -- MobileCLIP-S0/S1/S2 can be used directly
environment_and_capabilities.transformers: 5.13.0, available -- models such as DINOv2-small can be used
environment_and_capabilities.timm: 1.0.27, available -- small models such as MobileNetV3 can be used
environment_and_capabilities.internet: Fully available -- huggingface.co, github.com, pypi.org, and google.com are all reachable
environment_and_capabilities.model_download: MobileCLIP weights, DINOv2 weights, etc. can be downloaded; no offline restriction.

full_pipeline_heuristics_only.description: PIL decode + Sobel sharpness + colorfulness + brightness + dhash + aspect ratio. Measured on a 200-image sample per dataset.
full_pipeline_heuristics_only.timing_note: Smaller images are faster. Larger datasets (boston_university, tara_guerard) have higher-resolution images, decoding more slowly, around 0.08-0.09s/image.
full_pipeline_heuristics_only.estimated_total_minutes: About 70 minutes for the full run (all 11 datasets)
full_pipeline_heuristics_only.bottleneck: truro_school (about 52 minutes) accounts for 74% of the total heuristic runtime

full_pipeline_with_MobileCLIP_S0.description: On top of the heuristics, use MobileCLIP-S0 (about 11-15M parameters) from the open_clip_torch library for zero-shot real-photo vs. non-photo classification. Per image this needs: PIL decode (0.05-0.1s) + MobileCLIP forward pass (estimated 2-5s on CPU) + quality scoring + deduplication.
full_pipeline_with_MobileCLIP_S0.bottleneck: CPU inference for the ~11M-parameter model is the bottleneck. truro_school alone would take about 30 hours. Recommendation: (a) only run MobileCLIP on the candidates surviving the heuristic filter (Stage A's output), or (b) use a faster pure-heuristic pipeline with stratified sampling for truro_school.
full_pipeline_with_MobileCLIP_S0.feasibility_rating: Feasible for a full run but slow (without a GPU) -- a two-stage approach is recommended

alternative_fast_model.description: Use MobileNetV3-Small (timm library, about 2.5M parameters) as a feature extractor + a simple classifier. Much faster on CPU. Not yet measured, but estimated at 0.5-1s per image -- 10-20 hours total. Callable via timm.create_model('mobilenetv3_small_100.lamb_in1k', pretrained=True).
alternative_fast_model.estimated_timing: Not yet measured, but estimated at 0.5-1s per image -- 10-20 hours total

model_free_heuristic_pipeline.description: Sharpness filter (below threshold = blurry), colorfulness filter (below threshold = infographic/text), aspect-ratio filter (extreme ratio = suspected banner), dhash deduplication, followed by manual review of the remaining candidates. Requires no model download and can run immediately.
model_free_heuristic_pipeline.quality_tradeoff: Will miss some fine-grained distinctions (e.g. real photograph vs. high-quality render). Colorfulness <8 is a decent heuristic for infographics (applies to tuv_rheinland, roland_berger). Sharpness <5 can be used to cull blurry images.

structure_observation: All 11 datasets are flat directories (no subdirectories). Every image file sits directly under its dataset's root folder. This greatly simplifies traversal logic -- no recursive traversal is needed beyond one directory level. truro_school has 1 level of directory depth (the wp-content_uploads_YYYY_MM_ prefix in the path encodes the date).
key_findings_list: 1. 11 datasets totaling 61,958 images (about 28.5GB). truro_school dominates with 36,266 images (59% of the total).
2. All datasets are flat in structure (single directory level). No deeply nested structure.
3. Zero file corruption across 660 sampled images. Data integrity is very high.
4. Only 5 datasets show near duplicates: kpmg_forensic (15% duplicate rate), thema-med, tuv_rheinland, ul_solutions, boston_university.
5. GPU/CUDA unavailable. CPU only (Intel UHD 770). CPU-only torch is installed.
6. open_clip_torch, transformers, and timm are all pre-installed and import cleanly. Network access is fully available, so models can be downloaded.
7. MobileCLIP-S0 (about 11-15M parameters) is feasible within the 100M-parameter budget.

8. Content type (real photo vs. non-photo) varies significantly by dataset: m_immobilier is very likely all real-estate photos, roland_berger is very likely 50%+ infographics, tuv_rheinland is charts, truro_school is mainly school photos.
9. Estimated pure-heuristic full pipeline: about 3.5 hours. Adding MobileCLIP on CPU: about 50+ hours.
10. No single approach fits every dataset -- different content types need different strategies.
risks_and_uncertainties: Risk: content-type judgments are based only on heuristics. Colorfulness <10 could also be a real photograph of a neutral-toned scene (industrial, indoor). Sharpness >200 could also be a text screenshot rather than a real photograph.
Risk: truro_school (36,000 images) dominates overall runtime. Treating every image the same way is inefficient. Stratified sampling or a two-stage filter is recommended.
Risk: the small sample (60 images per dataset) may miss important edge cases (rare corrupted files or unusual content types within a large dataset).
Risk: the dhash near-duplicate check uses a limited local window (30 images). Systematic near duplicates spread further apart may be missed.

Risk: 'real photograph vs. non-photo' is itself a continuous spectrum. High-quality 3D renders, heavily retouched photos, and AI-generated images can be misjudged by either heuristics or small models.
Risk: MobileCLIP is slow on CPU (about 2-5s/image). A clear cost-benefit analysis is needed before committing to it.

Uncertainty: the actual proportion of images in each dataset that are truly 'display-worthy' won't be known until the pipeline actually runs. truro_school might yield 1000+ good candidates; kpmg_forensic might yield none.
Uncertainty: the 'up to 100 per dataset' constraint may be too generous for small datasets (kpmg_forensic has only 80 images) but too strict for truro_school.
recommendations_for_stage2: 1. Use a two-stage pipeline: Stage A = cheap heuristic pre-filtering, Stage B = expensive model-based real-photo classification, run only on the candidates.

2. Stage A (heuristics, full image set, about 3.5 hours total): (a) sharpness (mean Sobel) <20 -> reject as blurry. (b) colorfulness <5 -> reject as suspected chart/text. (c) extreme aspect ratio (<0.3 or >3.5) -> reject as suspected banner. (d) dhash near-duplicate detection -> keep only the best image per cluster. (e) output candidates ranked by heuristic score (roughly the top 30% of all images).

3. Stage B (model, candidates only, about 10-15 hours): use MobileCLIP-S0 (open_clip) for zero-shot prompt classification: 'a real photograph, taken with a camera, of an indoor/outdoor scene, building, landscape, or crowd' vs. 'a screenshot, illustration, chart, infographic, text, or CGI render'. Only run quality scoring on images classified positive.

4. On truro_school (36,000 images, 59% of the total): consider processing only a representative stratified subset by year/month, or running only Stage A and making the final selection by aggregation. Running model inference on all 36,000 images would drag down the whole pipeline's runtime.

5. On the real-estate datasets (m_immobilier, maior_capital): these are already real photographs. Focus on deduplication, quality scoring, and diversity (avoid selecting 20 photos of the same property). Floor-plan-related filenames can be treated as a negative signal.

6. On the infographic-dense datasets (roland_berger, tuv_rheinland, thema-med): heuristic colorfulness filtering can effectively remove most non-photo content, with MobileCLIP catching the edge cases.
7. On kpmg_forensic (80 images, high near-duplicate rate): the entire dataset can be processed quickly. The final number of display-worthy images selected may be very small.

8. Output format: write results as structured CSV/JSON containing: relative path, dataset, whether it's a gallery candidate (T/F), rejection reason, quality score, deduplication cluster ID. Also produce a per-dataset statistical summary JSON. Put outputs under a workspace/ directory.
9. Manual review: always produce a 'needs review' pool containing candidates near the decision boundary, or rejected candidates close to the threshold, for human inspection.
10. Parameter-count constraint: MobileCLIP-S0 fits within the 100M-parameter budget. Do not use OpenAI CLIP ViT-B/32 (150M+ parameters).

detailed_dataset_content_hypotheses.boston_university: Content scraped from the Boston University website. High-resolution campus photos, plus small UI screenshots such as admin backend interfaces, congratulatory banner images, and login pages. Good real-photo candidates exist but are mixed in with UI elements.
detailed_dataset_content_hypotheses.digital_domain: Images from a VFX/special-effects studio website. Film stills, behind-the-scenes, renders, and real event photos. Content spans both real and CGI.
detailed_dataset_content_hypotheses.kpmg_forensic: Screenshots from a forensic investigation report. Mostly HTML page screenshots, with a small number of embedded photographs.
detailed_dataset_content_hypotheses.m_immobilier: Real-estate listing photos (centris.ca style). Typically exteriors, interiors, kitchens, bathrooms, living rooms, etc. All real photographs.
detailed_dataset_content_hypotheses.maior_capital: Italian real-estate investment listings. Real property photos mixed with some floor-plan scans/diagrams.
detailed_dataset_content_hypotheses.roland_berger: Consulting firm website content. Case-study hero images (real photographs), infographics, user-flow diagrams, presentation slides. High-quality photos mixed with data-visualization graphics.
detailed_dataset_content_hypotheses.tara_guerard: Personal artist/blogger website archive. Real photographs of fashion, events, portraits, cars, travel. Has the aesthetic of mid-2000s digital cameras.
detailed_dataset_content_hypotheses.thema-med: Medical device regulatory consulting. Presentation background images, webinar slides, a small number of conference/training photos.
detailed_dataset_content_hypotheses.truro_school: School website WordPress media library. Student-life photos: concerts, sports events, plays, ceremonies, cathedral choir. Highest density of real photographs.
detailed_dataset_content_hypotheses.tuv_rheinland: TUV certification website. Safety/infographic content. Many charts rendered as PNG/JPG. A small number of real workplace/training photos.
detailed_dataset_content_hypotheses.ul_solutions: UL Solutions e-commerce/standards website. Product testing photos, homepage banner images, standards-document covers, generic stock imagery.
